messages.subject: Help.....
parts:
st1\:*{behavior:url(#default#ieooui) }
Dear all,



We are using Distance 5.0 for estimating the population abundance of an endemic wild sheep in the island of Cyprus. We find some difficulties running the program and we would like to ask for your assistance.



The line transects that we are using are in a mountain range. Each line is surrounded by high hills in both left and right site; therefore the visibility is up to 400-500 meters left and right. How can this parameter be included in the program? i.e. is there any difference in the total area we are going to use or not?



Generally, we have several line transects with various length. By using the perpendicular distance and a laser, the distances from the transect of all the wild sheep seen were recorded (female, male, young and newborn were put in different classes in the programme).



We put the numbers of each record in a cluster i.e. the individuals recorded at a distance of 300 m were summed into one record and the cluster was given the summed number. The data was separated into two strata (forest edge and forest core); the area of these strata, the line transects, the line lengths, the clusters and the four separate animal classes were included and the project was created. Then an analysis was run (CDS, no stratification, all key functions and AIC were used)



However, the output shows much fewer animals than the expected (from rough estimations)....

Can anyone help???



Thanks in advance
